result: HepG4-seq is a novel antibody-free method for mapping native G4s in living cells. The method uses hemin-induced proximal biotinylation of G4s and was validated by showing specific biotinylation signals, minimal effect on G4 folding, identification of 6,799 consensus peaks in HEK293 cells, overlap with predicted G4-forming sequences, and detection of dynamic G4s upon helicase inhibition.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge HepG4-seq as 'a useful antibody-free method to map G-quadruplexes' and note 'the development and optimization of HepG4-seq...offer novel methods to map native G4s.' While one reviewer states the comparison to existing datasets 'does not unequivocally demonstrate the superiority,' the method itself and its basic functionality are accepted.

result: HBD-seq is an optimized method for mapping native R-loops that revealed 42,488 consensus peaks with high signal-to-noise ratio in HEK293 cells, with signals dramatically diminished by RNase treatment.
evaluation: Reviewers express concerns about HBD-seq specificity. One reviewer states 'The sensitivity of the HBD-seq signals to a combination of RNase A and RNase H does not demonstrate that HBD-seq specifically reports the presence of RNA:DNA hybrids' and notes 'Legitimate concerns regarding the specificity of the Cut&Tag signals were not addressed.' Another reviewer questions whether 'HBD-seq did not perform satisfactorily and its binding specificity was questionable.'

result: Co-localized G4s and R-loops were identified in HEK293 cells (5,030 peaks) and mESCs (68,482 peaks), showing cell-type-specific distribution patterns. In HEK293 cells, 73.8% localized at promoters, 5'UTR, exon1, and intron1, while in mESCs the distribution was more diverse with enrichment at active promoters and enhancers of transcriptionally active genes.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the study 'provides extensive data on the distribution of G4s and R-loops, highlighting their co-localization in human and mouse cells' and that it 'identified dynamic, cell-type-specific distributions of co-localized G4s and R-loops.' The datasets are described as 'a good starting point for future functional studies,' indicating acceptance of the descriptive findings.

result: Inhibition of helicases BLM or WRN with small molecules resulted in significant accumulation of G4s and differential expression of hundreds of genes linked to co-localized G4s and R-loops, with enrichment in processes related to cell cycle, DNA metabolism, and DNA damage response.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise specific concerns about these findings. The data on helicase inhibition effects are part of the accepted descriptive characterization of G4 dynamics, though reviewers note the work 'remains primarily descriptive.'

result: Co-localized G4s and R-loops in mESCs overlap with active chromatin markers (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K36me3, H3K4me1) and RNAP, with distinct patterns at active promoters (18,496 peaks), bivalent promoters, active enhancers (15,787 peaks), poised enhancers, and unmarked enhancers.
evaluation: These chromatin mark associations are part of the accepted descriptive characterization. Reviewers acknowledge the study 'provides extensive data on the distribution of G4s and R-loops' without challenging these specific chromatin overlap findings.

result: Dhx9 is a key regulator of co-localized G4s and R-loops in mESCs. Loss of Dhx9 resulted in differential G4s and R-loops signals, with 65.5% of Dhx9 binding peaks overlapping with co-localized G4s and R-loops. Dhx9-bound differential peaks were linked to 852 genes with altered expression enriched in developmental processes, including key regulators like Nanog, Lin28a, Bmp4, Wnt8a, Gata2, and Lef1.
evaluation: The editor notes 'the strength of the evidence that DHX9 interferes with the ability of mESCs to differentiate by regulating directly the stability of either G4s or R-loops has been improved compared to a previous version, it is still incomplete.' Reviewers acknowledge 'the study consolidates the role of Dhx9 in modulating these structures' but express that 'the authors provide limited mechanistic insight into the major regulator of co-localized G4s and R-loops, helicase Dhx9.'

result: Loss of Dhx9 impaired the self-renewal and pluripotency of mESCs, as evidenced by altered expression of pluripotency markers (Lin28a, Oct4, Nanog), modest S-phase arrest, attenuated proliferation, and defects in embryoid body differentiation with differential expression of germ lineage markers.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge that the study 'reveals that the helicase Dhx9 can affect the self-renewal and differentiation capacities of mESCs' and 'explores its impact on mESC self-renewal and differentiation.' While mechanistic details are questioned, the phenotypic observations themselves are accepted.

result: Comparison of HepG4-seq with BG4 CUT&Tag showed 80% and 71% overlap in HEK293 cells and mESCs respectively. HepG4-seq peaks exhibited sharper shape and better resolution around PQS centers than BG4 CUT&Tag, with signal intensity differences between cell types possibly reflecting G4 conformation dynamics.
evaluation: One reviewer notes 'the comparison between the novel methods and existing ones is an important addition,' but another states 'The new Figure 9 comparing HepG4-seq to existing datasets does not unequivocally demonstrate the superiority of the Hemin-based strategy to map G4s.' The comparison data are acknowledged but their interpretation regarding method superiority remains contested.

result: Comparison of HBD-seq with S9.6 CUT&Tag and other R-loop mapping methods (MapR, GST-2xHBD CUT&Tag) showed similar peak numbers but HBD-seq generated ~80,000 extra peaks compared to S9.6 CUT&Tag and exhibited stronger signal intensities and sharper peak shapes than MapR and GST-2xHBD CUT&Tag.
evaluation: While one reviewer acknowledges 'the comparison between the novel methods and existing ones is an important addition,' concerns about HBD-seq specificity persist. One reviewer notes 'the reliability and accuracy of these methods are still debatable' and questions whether HBD-seq 'did not perform satisfactorily.' The comparison data are presented but do not resolve underlying specificity concerns.

result: HepG4-seq is capable of robustly and specifically capturing native G4s with high sensitivity, as demonstrated by detection of 6,799 peaks under wild-type conditions and 77,003 peaks with helicase inhibition.
evaluation: Reviewers describe HepG4-seq as 'a useful antibody-free method' and acknowledge 'the development and optimization of HepG4-seq...offer novel methods to map native G4s.' The basic capability and sensitivity of the method are accepted, though superiority claims are questioned.

result: Endogenous co-localized G4s and R-loops are prevalently present in regulatory regions of active genes and are involved in transcriptional regulation of their linked genes.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the study shows co-localized structures 'predominantly localize at active promoters and enhancers of transcriptionally active genes' and accept the descriptive characterization, though they note the work 'remains primarily descriptive' and 'does not substantially add to existing publications.'

result: Only a fraction (4,060 of 47,857) of Dhx9-bound co-localized G4s and R-loops displayed differential signals upon Dhx9 loss, suggesting redundant regulators exist. Loss of Dhx9 altered expression of 30 helicases/regulators, half of which form physical interaction networks, highlighting the complexity and redundancy of G4 and R-loop regulation.
evaluation: These findings on regulatory complexity and redundancy are accepted as part of the descriptive characterization. Reviewers acknowledge the study addresses 'the interplay between G-quadruplexes (G4s) and R-loops' and the complexity of their regulation, though they note limited mechanistic insight.
